set.n: Gold coins in a white ash on the Millet farm, Lexington Twp (part found 1906; the 1858 Reinhart murder)
set.pl: Martin Millet farm, Lexington Twp, Le Sueur Co (1906 find); farm not yet on a plat
set.st: May 1906: the Huber brothers, sawing a large white-ash log from the Martin Millet farm in Lexington Twp, found seven $20 gold pieces (latest dated 1854) in a bored, plugged hole. Old settlers tied it to a man lynched at Lexington in 1858-59 for murdering a German land-seeker. The German was said to carry about $600, so $140 surfaced in 1906 and the rest is unaccounted for. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself. A La Crosse Tribune special quotes Alderman William Grover tying the gold to the 1858 murder of a young German, robbed of about $600 in gold, by a neighbour named Reinhart, who was lynched; the gold was not found then.
src: Minneapolis Tribune (Star Tribune) 19 May 1906 p1 (TN TreasureNet Treasure Legends - Minnesota thread 714572)
La Crosse Tribune, 19 May 1906 (Special), 'Finding of Gold Recalls Early Hanging'
Duluth News Tribune, 8 May 1906, p. 2, "Sawyers Find Gold Imbedded in a Tree" (Le Sueur Center, May 7) (Newspapers.com 1126669191)
set.t: Part found 1906 ($140); the balance of the German's ~$600, if it exists, is unplaced. Private farm.
pinev: Lexington Twp (T111N R24W) centre, from BLM PLSS section corners; the Duluth News Tribune 1906 original names the Martin Millet farm in Lexington Twp. Farm not yet placed on a plat (PC (b) LIST 27 add-on).
set.tovw: Local original read; $140 recovered 1906; remainder legend
